about_blocks.text: Shifa Therapy is an online counselling service that matches Muslim clients with Muslim therapists, psychologists and counsellors. Its Google listing gives an office address at 5800 Ambler Drive in Mississauga, but the therapy itself happens by video. There are no beds, no detox and no residential stays, so this is outpatient care you fit around work, school and family.

about_blocks.text: The service describes its work as faith-centred and grounded in evidence-based therapy. Therapists are expected to understand Islamic values, family expectations and the stigma many Muslims feel about asking for help. Clients pick a therapist by concern, language and gender, and the site says people of other faiths are welcome too.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Shifa Therapy

faqs.question: Is Shifa Therapy a residential rehab?

answer_blocks.text: No. Shifa Therapy is an online outpatient counselling service, and sessions take place by video from wherever you are. It has no beds, no detox and no overnight stays. If you need medically supervised withdrawal or a live-in program, look at residential centres in Mississauga, the GTA or elsewhere in Ontario, and consider Shifa Therapy for counselling alongside or after that care.

faqs.question: Does Shifa Therapy help with addiction?

answer_blocks.text: Yes, it offers online addiction counselling with Muslim therapists. Several therapists on the platform list substance abuse and addiction as a specialty, including alcohol and drug use, and gambling addiction is among the focus areas they name. Counselling is talk therapy such as CBT and ACT; the service does not prescribe medication or manage withdrawal.

faqs.question: How much does Shifa Therapy cost?

answer_blocks.text: A single 50-minute session costs US$80 to US$275, depending on the therapist's years of experience. Prepaid packs of 4, 8, 12 or 24 sessions lower the price, down to US$60 a session for the least experienced tier in a 24-session pack. Prices are in US dollars and are published on the Shifa Therapy pricing page, and the site says unused sessions do not expire.

faqs.question: Can I use OHIP or my work benefits?

answer_blocks.text: OHIP does not cover these sessions, and Shifa Therapy does not bill any insurer directly. After you pay, it emails a detailed receipt that you can submit to your extended health benefits. Canadian plans usually reimburse only when the therapist holds a registration the plan recognises, so check with your insurer before you book.

faqs.question: Are the therapists registered in Ontario?

answer_blocks.text: Not all of them. Shifa Therapy says its therapists are licensed in their home countries, and many practise from outside Canada. Some list Canadian credentials, such as a Canadian Certified Counsellor and Registered Psychotherapist (Qualifying), or a registered psychotherapist. Ask the team about a therapist's registration, or search the College of Registered Psychotherapists of Ontario register, before your first session.

faqs.question: What does faith-centred therapy mean at Shifa Therapy?

answer_blocks.text: It means your therapist is Muslim and is expected to respect Islamic values while using standard, evidence-based methods. The site gives examples such as waswasa, halal boundaries and family expectations as things therapists understand from their own lives. You can choose a male or female therapist and a session language, and clients of other faiths are welcome.

faqs.question: How do I book a session?

answer_blocks.text: You book online through the Shifa Therapy website. A three-question quiz about your concern, preferred therapist gender and language suggests matched therapists, then you choose one, pay by card and pick a time slot. Sessions last 50 minutes by video on a phone, tablet or laptop, and you can reschedule with at least 24 hours' notice. Support is available on WhatsApp at +1 226 828 9306 or by email at support@shifatherapy.com.

faqs.question: What if I am in crisis?

answer_blocks.text: Shifa Therapy does not provide emergency care. If you or someone else is in danger, call 911. In Canada you can also call or text 9-8-8 at any time to reach the Suicide Crisis Helpline.
